patients.label: Boy with autism spectrum disorder and white matter signal abnormalities followed from 38 to 66 months of age

identity_evidence.quote: a boy exhibiting both ASD and WMSAs

attribution_limitations: A first BERA at 29 months reported a deficit of auditory perception in the right ear and a diagnosis of unilateral hyperacusis sensorineuralis was recorded; repeated BERA at 36 and 38 months showed an average hearing threshold bilaterally, and the otolaryngologist considered the first finding possibly influenced by EEG instability.
Start of therapy: the first examination paragraph says integrative therapy began immediately at 38 months, while the study design says treatment started a few days after the initial evaluation.
The MRT sentence in the paragraph headed by neurological status at 30 months carries no time of its own, and the MRT described by the otolaryngologist is not identified as the same study.
The article reports white matter signal abnormalities as a diagnosis and separately reports small scarring lesions on MRT; it does not state that the lesions are the abnormalities.
Several admission-visit and 66-month descriptive sentences have no time of their own beyond the first sentence of their paragraph, so only that first sentence is timed.
Table 2 prints the TIQ row label followed by "Age in months", although TIQ is an IQ value; the SEPAC rows are estimated ages in months.

The Results text gives SEPAC developmental lags (39, 33 and 24 months) without a time point, while the Discussion gives lags at 38 and 66 months; the source does not identify them as the same measurement.
The Discussion says ADOS-2 showed a slight decrease from 44 months, while Table 2 prints the same ADOS-2 score at t0 and t1 and a lower score from t2.
